item.title: EE.UU. y Canadá esbozarán un plan comercial en las próximas semanas: Carney
item.description: La actualización de Carney, publicada en una red social, se produjo dos días antes de la jornada electoral de las elecciones intermedias de EE.UU..
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Hughes
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — El primer ministro Mark Carney ha declarado que ha hablado con el presidente Donald Trump y que ambas partes trabajarán en un acuerdo comercial “mutuamente beneficioso” entre Estados Unidos y Canadá en las próximas semanas. La actualización de Carney, publicada en una red social, se produjo dos días antes de la jornada electoral de las elecciones intermedias de EE.UU., en las que la mayoría de las encuestas sugieren que es probable que los demócratas obtengan el control de la Cámara de Representantes, mientras que el Senado, que en su día se consideró un bastión republicano, se considera prácticamente una moneda al aire. Ver más: Negociaciones comerciales entre EE.UU. y Canadá cobran impulso, pero siguen sin acuerdo, dice Carney La semana pasada, Carney recibió a representantes de la Unión Europea en Montreal como parte de sus esfuerzos por estrechar los lazos con socios comerciales no estadounidenses. Carney no dio más detalles sobre su conversación con Trump, limitándose a señalar que se basaba en “recientes debates constructivos” sobre las líneas generales de un acuerdo que crearía puestos de trabajo, mejoraría la capacidad de compra de las familias y “respetaría plenamente las lenguas, la cultura y la soberanía de Canadá”. “Nuestros equipos trabajarán ahora durante las próximas semanas para lograr ese resultado”, afirmó. La Administración Trump acoge con satisfacción el compromiso continuo con Canadá mientras se trabaja para cerrar un acuerdo que tenga efectos significativos, declaró un portavoz de la Casa Blanca. Ver más: Trump amplía exenciones arancelarias a productos de Canadá para favorecer la campaña republicana en Maine Tras la reunión con la UE, Carney insinuó en una entrevista que el resultado de las elecciones de mitad de mandato no tendría un impacto significativo a la hora de modificar la postura política de Trump. Las negociaciones comerciales se rompieron en agosto cuando el enviado de Carney se retiró del acuerdo, en parte debido a una disputa sobre si ampliar la exención arancelaria propuesta por EE.UU. a los vehículos de carga media y pesada, algo que Canadá solicitaba. Canadá también acusó a EE.UU. de intentar restringir el uso del francés, una de las dos lenguas oficiales de Canadá. EE.UU. lo ha negado. Con la colaboración de Josh Wingrove. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

Iran, Qatari mediators hold third day of talks to end US-Iran war

Speaking to state media, Araqchi said discussions on a "two-day proposal" were continuing, but that no final conclusion had been reached.

Iran ian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday (Nov 1) for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran , an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters. The talks come amid concerns that the conflict could escalate again after the Nov 3 US midterm elections. President Donald Trump has said the United States will not launch new attacks on Iran before the vote and that talks with Tehran have been productive, though he has not ruled out further military action afterwards. Iran 's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" talks was to continue consultations with the Qatari mediators, adding Tehran is prepared for "both defence and diplomacy". Speaking to state media, Araqchi said discussions on a "two-day proposal" were continuing, but that no final conclusion had been reached.

Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera quoted Araqchi as saying in an interview on Saturday that Iran ian and Qatari negotiators had developed a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days of a potential agreement with Washington.

Related:

Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries, as the eight-month-old war continues to disrupt global oil supplies and spill over across the Middle East. "We are doing our best in this process, and we hope that there is rationality on the other side so that they prioritise diplomacy over other paths," Araqchi said of the talks with Qatari officials. Iran 's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday ordered the armed forces to be prepared for any attack, while the military later announced steps to strengthen its readiness. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against Iran , but would prefer to resolve the conflict diplomatically. Qatari mediators were in Tehran on Friday for discussions with Iran ian officials before moving the talks to Doha on Saturday, an official had told Reuters. The talks were being coordinated in regular contacts with Washington, the official added.

Source: Reuters/fs

LIVERPOOL, England, Nov 1 : If Arsenal's title rivals thought their humbling penalty shoot-out defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood Town in the League Cup might have shaken the confidence of Mikel Arteta's side, Sunday's gritty 1-0 win at Liverpool would have been sobering viewing. Being knocked out by a team 84 rungs lower on the ladder was not the best way for Arteta's Premier League champions to prepare for a trip to Anfield, especially with Andoni Iraola's team beginning to click. Four days later, however, Arsenal's armour-plating looked fully restored as they held Liverpool at bay and sealed a first league win at Anfield for 14 years to move three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table. Kai Havertz's 16th-minute tap-in proved decisive as Liverpool, for all their attacking intent and 16 goal attempts, could not break down Arsenal's impregnable yellow wall.

"We just said after the last few days, after the defeat against Fleetwood, that things happen for a reason and that's going to give us another spring and hunger and belief to go and do it. What the team has done here today is incredible," Arteta, part of the Arsenal team that won 2-1 at Anfield in 2012, said. "(Liverpool) are in a really good moment. It was really deserved, to come here and win in the manner that we have done, I think the players deserve so much credit." Liverpool, seeking a third league win on the spin which would have moved them within three points of Arsenal, responded well to going behind with Florian Wirtz curling a free kick against the crossbar and Alexis Mac Allister heading a good chance over the crossbar before halftime. The hosts also felt they should have had a penalty when Jurrien Timber grabbed at Alexander Isak's shirt. But after the break the hosts rarely looked like breaking through a relentless Arsenal rearguard and their frustration boiled over with Mac Allister involved in an altercation with Noni Madueke and falling theatrically to the floor after a slight touch of foreheads. Despite the setback, Liverpool manager Iraola said there were plenty of positives. "I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down. We finished the first half very well, kept pushing. I loved a lot of moments of the game," he said. "We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. Arsenal are in the best of the situations but it is just the start of November today. A lot of games to play." On whether his side should have had a penalty, he was in no doubt, suggesting Isak's honesty in not falling over after being held by Timber had worked against him. "There is a clear grab of the shirt. Alex was just in front of him, he was going to head in front of the goal but couldn't because he had the shirt," he said. "I don't understand why they didn't call it, probably because he has not gone to the floor."

Source: Reuters

FAST

LIVERPOOL, England, Nov 1 : Champions Arsenal moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League with Kai Havertz's early goal securing a statement 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. German striker Havertz tapped in from Declan Rice's low cross in the 16th minute after the hosts were caught trying to play the ball out of their defence. Liverpool responded strongly as halftime approached with Florian Wirtz curling a free kick against the crossbar and Alexis Mac Allister heading a good chance over the bar. But Arsenal weathered the storm and defended superbly to keep Liverpool largely at arm's length after the break and seal their first Premier League win at Anfield for 14 years.

Mikel Arteta's side replaced Manchester City at the top with 24 points from nine games, with City on 21 after losing at home to Brighton and Hove Albion on Saturday, their second successive league defeat after winning their first seven. Liverpool's second league defeat of the season left them nine points behind Arsenal in fifth place. For all Liverpool's huff and puff they failed to register an effort on target as Arsenal smothered their hosts with the kind of gritty away display that has become Arteta's blueprint. 'CRAZY STAT' Arsenal were stunned by fourth-tier Fleetwood Town in the League Cup in midweek but normal service was restored as they frustrated Liverpool to record a sixth clean sheet in nine league games and the significance of the win was clear in the way their players celebrated in front of their joyous fans. "This means a lot to the whole football club and it's been 14 years, that is a crazy stat and I think that we are all happy that we gave it to them today," Havertz said. "I think we all know what this stadium is about and what the fans are about. Liverpool have big players and they can show their quality. We knew that this was coming for us and we all stuck together and defended together." Liverpool have slowly found their rhythm this season under Andoni Iraola and victory on Sunday would have raised hopes of them being genuine title contenders. But after back-to-back league wins they got a reality check and could have few complaints. Liverpool were architects of their own downfall as they ceded possession to Arsenal's press and when the ball was played out to Noni Madueke he found the overlapping Rice who slid a pass across for Havertz to end his nine-game goal drought. Iraola's team dominated the rest of the half and had a strong penalty shout turned down when Jurrien Timber grabbed at Alexander Isak's shirt. But Arsenal tightened up in the second half and denied the hosts any clear sights at goal. "That is the Anfield way, that is what this Liverpool team can do and they just create waves and waves of attack. Relentless attacks," the tireless Rice said. "We knew it wouldn't have been easy but in the end that defensive line and that togetherness is undefeated. "So happy for Havertz because he deserved that goal and ultimately the 1-0 win."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Programas de informática pierden alumnos en EE.UU. mientras la IA sustituye puestos de trabajo
item.description: El auge de la inteligencia artificial ha dificultado en los últimos años que los titulados en informática encuentren empleo, ya que las empresas están eliminando muchos puestos de programación.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Rembert
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Los departamentos de informática y ciencias de la información de las universidades estadounidenses han sufrido una fuga de estudiantes este otoño, con un descenso de las matriculaciones de más del 12% en los programas de grado y de más del 10% en los de posgrado. Estas pérdidas se suman a la caída registrada el año pasado, que invirtió la tendencia de crecimiento que los programas de informática habían experimentado durante años, según los datos preliminares de matriculación de otoño del National Student Clearinghouse publicados este jueves. Ver más: EE.UU. se suma a la búsqueda de los responsables del hackeo a Binance que sucita un intenso escrutinio El auge de la inteligencia artificial ha dificultado en los últimos años que los titulados en informática encuentren empleo, ya que las empresas están eliminando muchos puestos de programación para principiantes. En agosto, un informe de la Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales reveló que los puestos de trabajo relacionados con la informática y las matemáticas serían los más afectados por la inteligencia artificial. En tan solo dos años, los programas de grado en informática han perdido el 18,4% de sus estudiantes, mientras que los programas de posgrado han perdido el 27,1%. “Se trata de descensos realmente notables para un campo que, hasta hace poco, era una de las áreas de más rápido crecimiento que habíamos observado en la educación superior”, afirmó Matthew Holsapple, director sénior de investigación del National Student Clearinghouse. Por su parte, la matriculación en carreras relacionadas con la salud creció hasta un 6,2% en todas las instituciones y tipos de titulación. Los resultados preliminares apuntan a “diferencias sustanciales en lo que estudian los alumnos”, señaló Holsapple. En términos más generales, la matriculación en estudios de grado en las universidades estadounidenses se estabilizó este otoño. El número de matriculados aumentó un 0,6%, lo que supone el cuarto año consecutivo de crecimiento, aunque se observa una desaceleración con respecto al incremento del 2,4% registrado en el otoño de 2025. La matriculación en programas de posgrado descendió un 1,6 %, impulsada por una caída del 3,7% en los programas de máster. Los datos preliminares del National Student Clearinghouse no incluyen información sobre la matriculación de estudiantes internacionales, que ha sido objeto de las políticas de inmigración del presidente Donald Trump. La matriculación de nuevos estudiantes extranjeros descendió un 17% en el otoño de 2025, según un análisis realizado por JB International y NAFSA, una organización estadounidense dedicada a la educación internacional. El informe definitivo, previsto para enero, incluirá cifras sobre la matriculación de estudiantes internacionales, pero los primeros indicios apuntan a que las pérdidas continuarán. Las solicitudes de admisión a universidades procedentes del extranjero se redujeron en torno a un 10% este año, lo que supone el mayor descenso en al menos una década, según la plataforma Common App. Ver más: Intel se desploma tras proyectar ventas inferiores a las estimadas por Wall Street Los centros de formación profesional son el único aspecto positivo. Estas instituciones registraron un aumento del 1,2% en la matriculación de grado, según el informe del National Student Clearinghouse. “Los estudiantes están identificando itinerarios que se adaptan a sus necesidades más allá de la vía tradicional”, afirmó Holsapple. “Y creo que la asequibilidad es, casi con toda seguridad, un factor importante en ello”. item.title: OPEC+ set to keep December oil output targets steady amid war disruption
item.description: Seven OPEC+ members are expected to hold December output targets steady as Gulf producers continue to face export disruptions from the US-Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OPEC+ oil-producing countries were set to keep oil production targets steady for December at a meeting on Sunday as the group continues to struggle with export disruptions from the US-Iran war. The seven core OPEC+ members have agreed in principle to keep output unchanged for next month, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Saturday, in line with expectations that further policy adjustments will not occur until next year. Sunday's online meeting of the seven countries — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — comes as Gulf members have been boosting exports that have been disrupted for months by the conflict. Most, however, are still pumping well below their targets. All of the people declined to be identified. The meeting starts at 1200 GMT, one of them said. OPEC+ comprises the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia. The group has been boosting output targets for much of 2026 and in September completed the phased rollback of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in 2023. At earlier meetings, it kept the targets steady for October and November. Reuters reported in July that OPEC+ was likely to make no changes to its targets during the fourth quarter as it turns its focus to 2027 quota negotiations. The group still has one more layer of production cuts of about 2 million barrels per day covering most members through the end of 2026. OPEC+ needs to complete a review of members' production capacity during the fourth quarter before setting the 2027 baselines that will determine future quotas and shape plans to unwind those cuts, sources have said.

FAST

Nov 1 : Coventry City are investigating footage appearing to show one of their supporters taunting Sunderland with a photo of late young supporter Bradley Lowery during their Premier League match, the club said on Sunday. Lowery, who died aged six in July 2017, suffered from a rare form of cancer which spreads rapidly across the body. He became known nationally as he accompanied the team in taking to the pitch before matches. British media reports said that a 14-year-old boy had handed himself in to West Midlands Police, who launched an investigation after footage circulated on social media appearing to show an individual in the Coventry section displaying an image of Lowery during Sunderland's 3-1 defeat on Saturday. "Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland," the club said in a statement.

Lowery, Bradley's mother, issued a statement on Sunday through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which supports children and families affected by serious illness. "As his (Bradley's) mam, this breaks my heart. Behind that photo is a little boy who was loved beyond measure," she said.  "I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad's family help him understand how hurtful his actions were."  Reuters has contacted Sunderland and West Midlands Police for comment.

SANTANDER, Spain, Nov 1 : Real Madrid cruised to a 3-0 win at Racing Santander in LaLiga on Sunday as goals from Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande secured their sixth successive victory in all competitions. Third-placed Real moved to within three points of leaders Barcelona and one of second-placed Atletico Madrid. Racing remain 16th, a point above the relegation zone. Buoyed by last week's Clasico victory, Jose Mourinho's side moved the ball sharply and delivered another assured performance. Mbappe opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 11th minute before combining neatly with Arda Guler, who sent Bellingham through 10 minutes later. Bellingham glided around Racing goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala and rolled the ball into an empty net.

Diomande made it 3-0 nine minutes before halftime, thundering a bouncing ball into the top corner. The Ivorian has scored four goals and provided three assists in his last six appearances. Racing competed well but rarely threatened, allowing Real to control a largely uneventful second half. Mbappe came closest to adding another goal when he struck the post on the hour. Real Madrid produced a disciplined defensive display, limiting the hosts to one shot on target as goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois enjoyed a quiet return after missing last week's game through illness. Mourinho praised Real Madrid's forwards for setting the tone of their defensive work. "When more attack-minded players put in the hard, sacrificial work, it sends a positive message to the rest of the team," the Portuguese manager told reporters. As Real Madrid continue on their upward trajectory, a satisfied Mourinho said his connection with his players was growing. "I’ve come to understand things that I didn’t grasp on the first day; the players have a better understanding of my character. "They understand what is non-negotiable for me. There’s a good human connection between the players and the coach. We’re in a good place," Mourinho added. Real Madrid next travel to AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday. Earlier on Sunday, Getafe came from behind to beat Sevilla 3-1.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Binance reanuda los retiros mientras persisten las dudas sobre el ataque informático
item.description: La mayor plataforma de activos digitales del mundo reanudó los retiros de bitcoins a partir de las 14:00 horas, hora de Singapur, más de dos días después de haberlos suspendido a raíz de la brecha de ...
item.dc:creator: Micah Barkley, Emma Haidar, Ryan Weeks
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Binance comenzó a restablecer los retiros de sus clientes el domingo, después de que unos piratas informáticos se llevaran más de US$6.000 millones en lo que constituye el mayor robo cibernético jamás registrado, mientras el sector de las criptomonedas espera respuestas sobre la brecha de seguridad atribuida a Corea del Norte y medidas para reforzar las defensas de la plataforma. La mayor plataforma de activos digitales del mundo reanudó los retiros de bitcoins a partir de las 14:00 horas, hora de Singapur, más de dos días después de haberlos suspendido a raíz de la brecha de seguridad. Al caer la tarde en Asia, la plataforma había registrado unas salidas netas de unos US$3.500 millones, según datos de DefiLlama. El coCEO, Yi He, afirmó en X que algunas transferencias se realizan entre carteras de Binance. Ver más: Binance recupera el 90% de las criptomonedas robadas y promete reactivar retiros el domingo La primera fase de retiradas abarca 15 tokens, entre los que se incluyen Ether y las dos mayores stablecoins: el USDT de Tether y el USDC de Circle Internet Group Inc., según informó Binance en X. Las retiradas en 15 redes blockchain, entre las que se incluyen Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, XRP y Base, se reanudaron alrededor de las 20:30 h en Singapur, según la empresa. Binance eclipsa a sus rivales del sector, con unos activos de aproximadamente US$132.000 millones, frente a los cerca de US$29.000 millones de OKX, la segunda mayor plataforma de intercambio. “Estamos adoptando un enfoque por fases, priorizando los tokens en función de los datos de la demanda de los usuarios de la semana pasada, de modo que cada red y cada par de activos puedan restablecerse con cuidado, tras completar las comprobaciones de estabilidad y seguridad antes de reabrir el acceso”, afirmó Binance. La empresa de negociación cuantitativa SQS Trading tiene aproximadamente una cuarta parte de su capital de negociación en Binance y está reduciendo esa cantidad en aproximadamente un tercio, según su fundador, Eli Williams, quien añadió que no liquidará posiciones ni reducirá el uso de la plataforma como lugar para la cobertura de riesgos. “Es difícil predecir cuál será el impacto neto en este momento, pero iremos supervisando las salidas de capital y el impacto en el volumen en comparación con otras plataformas importantes”, afirmó Williams. Otros están posponiendo cualquier cambio. Justin d’Anethan, director de investigación de Arctic Digital, una empresa de asesoramiento en mercados privados, afirmó que no le ha inquietado el ataque informático. “Cuando algo parece sospechoso, es bueno actuar con rapidez; pero cuando ocurre algo catastrófico, es mejor abstenerse de tomar medidas”, señaló. “No me he alejado de Binance ni lo haría”. Un portavoz de Binance señaló que los volúmenes de retirada “se dispararon al principio”, pero que ahora se están estabilizando en lo que la empresa considera una actividad normal, y que representan un pequeño porcentaje del total de sus activos gestionados. La reanudación pone a prueba la promesa de Binance de indemnizar íntegramente a los clientes tras un robo cuatro veces mayor que el anterior récord de ataque informático a una plataforma de criptomonedas, ocurrido en Bybit en 2025. La Oficina Federal de Investigación de EE. UU. (FBI) afirmó el sábado que el ataque a Binance fue perpetrado por TraderTraitor, una unidad de piratas informáticos de élite norcoreana a la que también responsabilizó del robo de aproximadamente US$1.500 millones en Bybit. Las repercusiones en el mercado parecen relativamente contenidas, ya que la mayoría de las principales criptomonedas registraron el domingo una variación inferior al 1%. El bitcoin, que representa alrededor del 60% del valor de mercado del sector, cotizaba en torno a los US$78.000, aproximadamente un 5% por debajo de su máximo del jueves, antes del ataque. “En cierto modo, esto demuestra lo mucho que ha madurado el sector”, afirmó Haseeb Qureshi, socio director del fondo de capital riesgo Dragonfly. “Hemos sido testigos de respuestas extraordinariamente rápidas”. Ver más: Binance estima en US$6.300 millones el mayor hackeo de la historia de las criptomonedas Binance ha declarado que, hasta la fecha, ha repuesto aproximadamente el 95% de las criptomonedas sustraídas utilizando su tesorería corporativa, fondos de emergencia y fondos de seguros. Los fondos sustraídos en el ataque eran una combinación de las principales criptomonedas de diez cadenas de bloques, entre las que se incluyen el bitcoin y el ethereum. “Nuestro compromiso sigue siendo el mismo: Binance asumirá el impacto financiero de los fondos sustraídos”, afirmó. “Estas pérdidas no se repercutirán a los usuarios”. La plataforma es capaz de cubrir las pérdidas gracias a su inversión continua de ingresos en criptomonedas, según declaró el coCEO de Binance, Richard Teng, en un vídeo publicado el viernes en las redes sociales. Yi He afirmó que los ingresos de Binance para este año cubrirían por completo la cantidad perdida. El coste final para Binance sigue sin estar claro. La plataforma de intercambio indicó que, a fecha de este viernes, se habían congelado unos US$3.000 millones en activos afectados, aunque eso no significa que se hayan recuperado. La oleada de ataques sufridos este año por empresas del sector de las criptomonedas y por el sector financiero en general ha avivado la preocupación de que la inteligencia artificial esté aumentando la eficacia de los piratas informáticos. Algunos expertos en seguridad creen que los piratas informáticos norcoreanos han incorporado herramientas de IA a su arsenal, lo que les ayuda especialmente en tareas de reconocimiento y de ingeniería social. Junto con el FBI, las empresas de inteligencia de blockchain TRM Labs, Chainalysis y Elliptic han señalado a los piratas informáticos de Corea del Norte como los responsables del ataque a Binance. Estos ataques han puesto de manifiesto debilidades de seguridad en un momento en que el sector de las criptomonedas se abre paso en las finanzas tradicionales. En septiembre se sustrajeron cientos de millones de dólares de Bitget. Los piratas informáticos también robaron más de US$100 millones en bitcoins de carteras protegidas por dispositivos de Coinkite Inc., mientras que la manipulación de dispositivos Ledger provocó pérdidas por valor de millones de dólares. Otros ciberataques recientes han afectado al mercado de predicciones Polymarket, a las entidades financieras surcoreanas Mirae Asset Global Investments y Daishin Securities, así como a la plataforma japonesa de comercio de divisas GMO Internet Group Inc. El viernes, Yi y Teng abordaron el posible daño a la reputación que podría causar el ataque. En un vídeo publicado en X, Yi prometió que Binance seguiría colaborando con las fuerzas del orden para localizar a los atacantes. La empresa se ha comprometido a reembolsar a todos los usuarios que hayan perdido fondos en el ataque. “No permitiremos que los piratas informáticos nos arrebaten el impulso que esta industria se merece”, afirmó en su vídeo, hablando en mandarín. “Por supuesto, hay aspectos en los que podríamos haberlo hecho mejor. Deberíamos haber invertido más en seguridad antes y haber establecido normas más estrictas. De cara al futuro, no escatimaremos esfuerzos, ya sea invirtiendo en seguridad o luchando contra los piratas informáticos”. Ver más: Hackeo a Binance 2026: qué es el fondo SAFU y cómo cubrirá las pérdidas de los usuarios a nivel global Binance creó en 2018 una reserva de emergencia denominada “Fondo de Activos Seguros para los Usuarios” (SAFU, por sus siglas en inglés), como medida de protección para los clientes en “situaciones extremas”, según la plataforma de intercambio. El SAFU se mantiene generalmente en torno a los US$1.000 millones, aunque en el pasado ha fluctuado en función de los movimientos del mercado, según indicó Binance en 2024. Binance había señalado anteriormente que el incidente podría estar relacionado con el ordenador portátil de un ingeniero de software que había sido comprometido, así como con “otros puntos de brecha de seguridad”. Según la empresa, no se encontraron pruebas de que se hubieran filtrado claves privadas. Con la colaboración de Muyao Shen. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: El shock electoral en Brasil expone los riesgos de las apuestas más populares en los mercados emergentes
item.description: El real sufrió el lunes su peor jornada desde 1999, mientras que la bolsa brasileña se vio obligada a suspender la cotización apenas unos minutos después de la apertura.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Wong
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La caída del mercado brasileño ha supuesto una severa advertencia para los inversores de los mercados emergentes: las operaciones con gran concentración de participantes pueden desmoronarse a una velocidad alarmante. Las apuestas más populares, que van desde las acciones asiáticas vinculadas a la inteligencia artificial hasta los bonos húngaros y el rand sudafricano, se enfrentan ahora a un nuevo escrutinio después de que una sorpresa electoral provocara la caída de las acciones brasileñas y del real, poniendo de manifiesto cómo un posicionamiento demasiado unilateral puede amplificar los giros del mercado. Ver más: El desplome de la bolsa de Brasil por Lula deja un contagio limitado en América Latina Allspring Global Investments considera que las acciones de inteligencia artificial, en las que hay una gran concentración de inversores, son vulnerables a una decepción en torno a la salida a bolsa de Anthropic, mientras que Invesco se muestra cautelosa ante los riesgos vinculados al gasto en inteligencia artificial de las grandes empresas tecnológicas. Société Générale SA señala el crédito de los mercados emergentes debido a los estrechos diferenciales, mientras que Citigroup Inc. ( C ) destaca las posiciones concentradas de los compradores en las tasas de interés húngaros y el florín, así como en la deuda de países fronterizos en moneda local. “Una postura restrictiva de la Reserva Federal o una escalada significativa de los conflictos geopolíticos podrían ejercer presión sobre las posiciones en mercados emergentes que han sido las favoritas de los inversores”, afirmó Brendan McKenna, estratega de mercados emergentes de Société Générale en Nueva York. Están surgiendo indicios de posiciones sobrecalentadas en todos los mercados. La posición larga neta de los fondos apalancados en el rand sudafricano se encuentra cerca de su máximo de los últimos dos años, mientras que las tenencias extranjeras de bonos húngaros han alcanzado un récord. Una encuesta realizada el mes pasado por Bank of America Corp. ( BAC ) reveló que las acciones de semiconductores a nivel mundial son la inversión más masificada. El real sufrió el lunes su peor jornada desde 1999, mientras que la bolsa brasileña se vio obligada a suspender la cotización apenas unos minutos después de la apertura. El índice de referencia cerró con una caída de casi el 14%, y algunas acciones perdieron más del 50%, ya que la inesperada reelección del presidente de izquierdas Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva trastocó los mercados, que en su mayoría estaban posicionados a favor de una victoria del candidato de derechas Flávio Bolsonaro. Antes del resultado, el real era la segunda divisa de los mercados emergentes con mejor rendimiento en lo que va de año, solo por detrás del peso colombiano, ya que las elevadas tasas de interés de Brasil atraían a fondos extranjeros en busca de rentabilidad, mientras que el repunte de los precios de las materias primas proporcionaba un apoyo adicional. “Como prueba de ello, basta con observar la magnitud de los daños que estamos presenciando estos días a raíz de la reelección sorpresa de Lula”, afirmó Julio Callegari, director de inversiones de renta fija para Asia en JPMorgan Asset Management, en una entrevista concedida el martes en Singapur. “Se trata de una gran sacudida en el valor en riesgo, ¿verdad? Yo diría que el mercado aún no se ha recuperado del todo". McKenna, de SocGen, señaló el crédito como una de las operaciones con mayor concentración de inversores. “Los diferenciales están muy ajustados”, especialmente en un contexto de elevada inflación, endurecimiento de la política monetaria por parte de los bancos centrales e incertidumbre geopolítica, afirmó. La prima de rendimiento del índice de bonos soberanos de mercados emergentes de Bloomberg respecto a los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense comparables se ha reducido a 210 puntos básicos, más de 100 puntos básicos por debajo de su media de cinco años, que es de 315. Mientras tanto, la agitación en Brasil también ha vuelto a centrar la atención en Hungría, uno de los países con mejor rendimiento de los mercados emergentes este año. Los activos locales se han recuperado, ya que el cambio de Gobierno ha avivado las esperanzas de avanzar hacia la adopción del euro. Las tenencias extranjeras de bonos y letras del Tesoro húngaros alcanzaron el mes pasado un récord de 11,1 billones de forints (US$34.000 millones), lo que pone de relieve el gran interés de los inversores por esta deuda. Del mismo modo, los fondos apalancados y las gestoras de activos mantienen unas posiciones largas netas de unos 688 millones de dólares en el rand sudafricano, cerca de su máximo desde finales de 2024, según muestran los datos de la Comisión de Comercio de Futuros de Materias Primas (CFTC) recopilados por Bloomberg. El rand ha figurado entre las operaciones de carry trade más populares de este año, una estrategia que consiste en obtener financiación en una moneda con tasas de interés bajos para invertir en activos de mayor rentabilidad. “Dado el aumento de la volatilidad de los activos de riesgo (especialmente en lo que respecta a las tasas de interés), el sector de la inversión se ha visto acorralado en unas pocas operaciones similares”, escribieron los estrategas de Citi en una nota reciente. “Si alguna de esas operaciones idiosincrásicas residuales resultara decepcionante, podríamos asistir a una aceleración de esta tendencia a reducir el riesgo”, añadieron. También en los mercados fronterizos, las operaciones en las que participan los fondos están siendo objeto de escrutinio. Carol Lye, gestora de fondos de Brandywine Global Investment Management en Singapur, señaló la saturación de posiciones en letras a corto plazo en moneda local de países fronterizos como Egipto, Turquía, Nigeria y Kazajistán. Si las tasas de interés mundiales suben mucho más, o si los mercados de valores comienzan a sufrir una corrección, “se observará una gran salida de capital rotativo de estas operaciones”, afirmó. Un indicador de JPMorgan que sigue la evolución de la deuda emitida por países fronterizos ha retrocedido alrededor de un 3% desde el máximo histórico alcanzado a principios de septiembre. Sin duda, la inestabilidad política y los cambios bruscos de tendencia en los mercados son riesgos habituales para los inversores en mercados emergentes. Y, a pesar de las preocupaciones sobre la concentración de posiciones, muchas de las operaciones más populares de este año siguen contando con el respaldo de factores como los atractivos rendimientos y los sólidos resultados empresariales. Mientras tanto, una operación muy demandada en los mercados emergentes que ha comenzado a mostrar fisuras es la de las acciones asiáticas vinculadas a la inteligencia artificial. Las acciones tecnológicas han sufrido una corrección debido a que los resultados de algunas megacapitalizaciones estadounidenses han decepcionado, y han aumentado las preocupaciones sobre si el gasto masivo en inteligencia artificial puede traducirse en beneficios sostenibles. “El gasto en IA de las hiperescaladoras sigue siendo un indicador clave a tener en cuenta”, afirmó William Yuen, director de inversiones de Invesco. “Cualquier desaceleración significativa podría debilitar las perspectivas de crecimiento de las empresas asiáticas de la cadena de suministro tecnológico”. Ver más: Wall Street revisa sus apuestas por Brasil tras la victoria de Lula y el desplome de los mercados Un indicador de Bloomberg sobre los valores vinculados a los semiconductores en la región, que se sitúa en el corazón de la cadena de suministro de hardware de IA, ha caído casi un 25% desde el máximo alcanzado en junio. “Dentro de la renta variable de los mercados emergentes, las acciones relacionadas con la IA y el factor de impulso siguen siendo operaciones relativamente masivas”, señaló Gary Tan, gestor de carteras de Allspring Global. “Un proceso de salida a bolsa de Anthropic poco brillante podría poner a prueba la confianza del mercado”. Con la colaboración de Masaki Kondo, Andras Gergely, Selcuk Gokoluk y Ruth Carson. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

Crew from NASA's simulated Mars mission emerges after 378 days in isolation

This picture taken October 8, 2025, shows Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) Mission 2 crew members Ross Elder, Matthew Montgomery, Ellen Ellis, and James Spicer posing before spending more than a year in isolation at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston. Nov 1 : The four members of a crew who took part in a simulated mission to Mars have emerged after 378 days in isolation at the US space agency's Johnson Space Center in Houston, an endeavor designed to help prepare for a possible future excursion by NASA astronauts to Earth's planetary neighbor. "It's been a hell of a year — analog astronauts living in captivity of our own free will," Ellen Ellis, the medical officer on the Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog, or CHAPEA, mission, said in remarks at Johnson Space Center after emerging with her three crewmates on Saturday. The four entered the 1,700-square-foot (158-square-meter) 3D-printed habitat on October 19, 2025, and performed tasks such as growing crops in simulated Martian soil and interfacing with NASA officials with delays recreating those inherent in interplanetary communications. NASA, which has explored Mars with robotic rovers and orbiting spacecraft, has ambitions for a human mission to Mars as early as the 2030s, with plans before that to return astronauts to the moon for the first time since 1972.

"We have a narrowing window of opportunity to maintain US preeminence in space," Ellis said. Ellis mentioned the service academy for space-related operations pursued by President Donald Trump's administration and plans for a lunar base. "Let's seize the initiative, lead with science that will benefit our economy and ensure our legacy in space for our children's children," Ellis said. The other crew members were mission commander Ross Elder, science officer Matthew Montgomery and flight engineer James Spicer. "For Mars, the risks are great," Elder said in remarks after emerging from isolation. "But through seeking understanding, strong vision and leadership, creativity, fortitude, hard work and incredible foundation, the goal of putting humans on Mars is not only achievable, but rather inevitable." The crew is set to participate in two weeks of post-mission evaluations and debriefing with NASA scientists. NASA has said it is looking for insight into what it takes for astronauts to adapt to the routines and demands of daily life on long-duration missions beyond Earth to keep them healthy, productive, and connected. This was NASA's second CHAPEA mission, with another four-person crew in isolation at Johnson Space Center for 378 days spanning 2023 and 2024. Vanessa Wyche, director of the Johnson Space Center, greeted the crew members when they exited isolation. Wyche said they managed to live with limited resources, maintain their habitat, and carry out simulated Mars operations.  Wyche also noted how the crew dealt with the simulated interplanetary communications, with lag times between sending messages and receiving responses. "These delays require patience, careful planning and greater independence — qualities that will be essential for future astronauts traveling millions of miles from home," Wyche said. Wyche said the lessons learned from the CHAPEA crew and their experiences will help pave the way for the missions first to the moon and "one day, Mars."

Source: Reuters

By Christoph Steitz and Tilman Blasshofer FRANKFURT/PEISSENBERG, Germany, Nov 1 (Reuters) – German ministers threatened tough penalties for looters and rioters who damaged stores and injured more than 100 police officers in Frankfurt overnight, while praising security forces for preventing wider violence.

Frankfurt emerged as the main flashpoint on Saturday after tens of thousands of people rallied in dozens of German cities to demand better education and lower living costs in protests organised by campaign group “Gen Z regelt” — “Gen Z takes charge”.

In the financial hub Frankfurt, hooded rioters damaged 17 stores, of which five were looted, Roman Poseck, interior minister of the state of Hesse, told a press conference on Sunday.

Show Full Article

He said police deployed 1,300 officers, with more than 100 injured in clashes. Police arrested 54 people aged between 13 and 29.

“I am shocked by what I have seen, and there is no point in sugar-coating it. Let me make this very clear: Things cannot go on like this,” Poseck said.

Poseck said most of those arrested were German nationals, adding that many of those involved in the disturbances were of an immigrant background, citing information from the police.

“Police currently estimate that they are dealing with between 1,000 and 1,500 violent troublemakers, predominantly from an immigrant background,” he added.

PROTESTERS THROW PETROL BOMBS AT POLICE

Frankfurt police reported violent disturbances including windows being smashed and petrol bombs, rocks and bottles being thrown at the emergency services.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, a member of the conservative Christian Social Union, said perpetrators would be identified and held to account.

“I expect there to be severe penalties. We are not prepared to accept, in the slightest, that such incidents and such rioting should take place here,” he told reporters on Sunday.

He accused “troublemakers from the immigrant community” of acting alongside left-wing extremists and other far-left groups, but did not provide evidence to support the claim or say which groups had joined the demonstrations.

Dobrindt said a policing strategy based on a large security presence and deployments across multiple locations had proved effective.

In France, protests continued largely peacefully for a third weekend after extensive riots and looting on October 17 damaged shops, public buildings and businesses.

Dobrindt said that border controls had been tightened ahead of the protests out of fear extremist groups from abroad could exploit them to stir riots.

(Reporting by Christoph Steitz, Tilman Blasshofer and Ayhan Uyanik; Editing by Alison Williams, Hugh Lawson and Ros Russell)

The 2024 champion Chepkirui was running all by herself when she crossed the line

NEW YORK, Nov 1 : Kenyan Sheila Chepkirui took back her New York City Marathon crown in two hours, 24 minutes and 36 seconds on Sunday, while Sweden's Andreas Almgren (2:06:01) won the men's race in his debut over the distance.  The 2024 champion Chepkirui was running all by herself when she crossed the line, two years after she held off compatriot Hellen Obiri, who finished third, a second slower than American Jess McClain (2:24:42).  The half-marathon world champion Almgren finished 13 seconds ahead of Italian Yemaneberhan Crippa, while Kamohelo Mofolo (2:06:26) of Lesotho was third. Defending champion Obiri and Chepkirui broke away from the lead pack with about four miles to go and Obiri ran on her opponent's heels for much of the final stretch of the course, hoping for more magic after breaking the course record last year.

Obiri had appeared all but assured of second spot on the podium, but let the silver medal slip through her fingers in the final moments, as McClain came out of nowhere to sprint past her and cross the line a second faster. "The last mile was really tricky and I had to be patient because I knew Hellen was really strong," said Chepkirui. "I had to really push up to the finish line." Marathon debutant Almgren looked to be a veteran over the distance as he hung in with a crowded lead pack through the famously demanding and hilly course. He pulled away from the defending champion Benson Kipruto with one mile left and waved his arms as he coaxed more cheers from the crowd after building a comfortable lead.  "When Benson starting picking up the pace with 5k left I just thought, 'I've got the legs today'," said Almgren, who cruised through the final metres. "You can't ask for a better debut... I'm about to start crying." There was a lot of anticipation surrounding Almgren's arrival in New York and he lived up to the hype as he became the first European man in three decades to triumph across the five boroughs, and said he planned to tackle the 26.2 miles again. "It's better than anything I could have ever imagined," he said. The race kicked off under pristine conditions the morning after Halloween, as bleary-eyed partygoers staggered back to their apartments while runners made the journey to the starting line for the year's final major. In the men's wheelchair race, Swiss Marcel Hug snared his eighth New York win through a thrilling sprint finish with rival Daniel Romanchuk, crossing the line a second ahead of the American in 1:28:14. Hug's compatriot Catherine Debrunner had no drama in the women's race, crossing the line in 1:40:02, while Tatyana McFadden (1:48:28) finished second after outlasting fellow American Susannah Scaroni (1:48:32).  Scaroni lined up on Staten Island after giving birth in August and her baby son Jonah was on hand for a celebratory photo after she crossed the finish line.

Source: Reuters

Nov 1 : Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1 6-4 to win the Vienna Open on Sunday, claiming his fourth title of the season and the 28th of his career, and extending his ATP 500 winning streak to 26 matches. The 23-year-old Spaniard arrived in Vienna on the back of titles in Doha and Tokyo and completed a perfect 16-0 record at ATP 500 events in 2026, capping another dominant week without dropping a set across his five matches. Alcaraz seized control from the opening stages, breaking De Minaur's serve in the first game and quickly establishing a double-break advantage as the Australian struggled to contain the world number two's intensity. The seven-time Grand Slam champion raced through the opening set 6-1, repeatedly punishing short balls and forcing errors from De Minaur.

Alcaraz will head to next week's Paris Masters brimming with confidence after his flying start to the European indoor swing, having already qualified for the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin. De Minaur, meanwhile, will turn his attention to Paris as he continues his push to qualify for the ATP Finals for a third consecutive year.

Nov 1 (Reuters) – Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) said on Sunday that a Russian minor had been detained over a threat to carry out a terrorist attack in a Moscow park following a tip-off from the United States, news agency Interfax reported.

On Saturday, the FSB said it had received information from the US through established partner channels about preparations for an attack in Moscow and was taking appropriate measures.

The minor had posted photographs of himself on TikTok wearing tactical clothing and a balaclava, holding an object that looked like an automatic weapon, as well as photographs taken at Moscow’s Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve with the caption: “I found a place,” Interfax cited the FSB as saying.

Show Full Article

“We are grateful to the American side for providing the information,” the security service was quoted as saying in its statement.

It said officials searching the minor’s home found the clothes and accessories seen in the social media posts, while his phone showed a subscription to a neo-Nazi channel on the app Telegram and “a significant number of searches concerning terrorist attacks, mass killings and other acts of violence,” according to Interfax.

Russia’s Investigative Committee is considering what legal or procedural action to take, the FSB said.

Tsaritsyno, a palace museum and park complex in southern Moscow, was temporarily closed on Saturday following the US tip-off.

(Reporting by Alessandra Prentice; Editing by Joe Bavier and Hugh Lawson)

LONDON, Nov 1 : Manchester City's Lauren Hemp struck the winner as her side beat London City Lionesses 2-1 away in a thrilling top-of-the-table clash in the Women's Super League on Sunday, with Hemp's decisive goal coming just after the Lionesses had equalised. The win briefly put City into first place but Chelsea reclaimed it later in the afternoon with a 6-0 thrashing of bottom side Charlton Athletic, who are still searching for their first point of the season.  Led by two goals from French striker Melvine Malard, Chelsea went back on top of the standings with 22 points after eight games, ahead of Manchester City on goal difference, with London City third on 16 points. The Lionesses had plenty of success with their high pressing in the first half but wasted the chances that came their way, and they were punished eight minutes into the second half when Bunny Shaw rounded keeper Mary Earps and kept a cool head before blasting the ball high into the net.

Jana Fernandez equalised for the home side with a brilliant glancing header from a corner in the 72nd minute, but she undid her good work just over two minutes later when she allowed Hemp to steal past her to stab home a cross from Mary Fowler for the winner.  In the other early kick-off, Arsenal's underwhelming start to the season continued when they were held to a 1-1 draw at home by Aston Villa, with Alessia Russo scoring the equaliser in the 85th minute to avoid another embarrassing defeat.  Tottenham Hotspur thumped Birmingham City 4-1 away to move up to fourth and bring a run of three straight league defeats to an end, while West Ham United secured an impressive home victory over Liverpool with the same scoreline.  Brighton & Hove Albion continued their solid start to the season with a 2-1 win over visitors Crystal Palace that put them sixth in the table on 11 points, one behind Manchester United, who played out a scoreless draw with Everton on Saturday.

Nov 1 : Bayern Munich's injury woes deepened when Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry were ruled out for an indefinite period, the club said on Sunday after both players were forced off in Saturday's 2-2 Bundesliga draw with Borussia Dortmund. • Saibari suffered a ligament tear in his right ankle after appearing to twist it during the match and has already undergone successful surgery. The Morocco international left the stadium on crutches following the incident • Gnabry was substituted just two minutes after Saibari's departure, with Bayern later confirming the German winger had suffered a muscle injury in his left thigh • Bayern also lost French playmaker Michael Olise to an apparent muscle injury late on in the match. • "Saibari and Gnabry will be missing from FC Bayern for the time being," the club said. "Saibari suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his right ankle joint and has already undergone successful surgery. Gnabry sustained a muscle injury in the posterior left thigh."

Source: Reuters

Nov 1 : Harriet Dart clinched the first WTA tour singles title of her career after battling back to beat Austrian Lilli Tagger 4-6 6-3 6-4 in the Guangzhou Open final on Sunday. • The British number five, ranked 115th in the world and coached by former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli, overcame a sluggish start after being broken in the opening game • Dart recovered to draw level at 4-4 in the first set but Tagger immediately broke again and served out the opener • The first break point of the second set went to Dart, who took it for 5-3 and then levelled the match, setting up a deciding set • In the final set, momentum swung repeatedly as the pair traded five consecutive breaks of serve. Dart finally steadied by saving two break points to hold for 5-3 and closed out the match to secure the title

item.description: LONDON/MOSCOW, Nov 1 : OPEC+ oil-producing countries kept December production targets steady on Sunday, confirming expectations that more policy adjustments will not occur until next year, as the group continues to struggle with export disruptions from the Iran war.Seven core OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, R

item.content:encoded:

OPEC+ keeps December oil output targets steady ahead of tougher call for 2027

OPEC logo is seen in this illustration taken June 25, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

FAST

LONDON/MOSCOW, Nov 1 : OPEC+ oil-producing countries kept December production targets steady on Sunday, confirming expectations that more policy adjustments will not occur until next year, as the group continues to struggle with export disruptions from the Iran war. Seven core OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — made the decision in an online meeting on Sunday, OPEC said in a statement. While Gulf members have been boosting exports that have been disrupted for months by the conflict, most are still pumping well below their targets. OPEC+ comprises the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia. Only the seven members — plus the United Arab Emirates until it quit OPEC in May — have been involved in monthly output decisions in recent years. All members of the 21-country group are due to meet on November 29, when analysts expect it will decide 2027 quotas. "Today's decision was the easy one," said Jorge Leon, an analyst at Rystad. "The much more important test comes at the November 29 ministerial meeting, when OPEC+ will decide its 2027 production framework."

Oil prices jumped more than 2 per cent on Friday, with Brent crude settling at almost $118 a barrel, the highest since April, as traders braced for a potential escalation in the Iran war after the US midterm elections. The International Energy Agency and other forecasters have warned of excess supply in 2027 should Gulf flows return to normal. "OPEC+ faces an extremely difficult call for 2027," Leon added. "The group has to plan around huge uncertainty over the US-Iran war, the pace of recovery through the Strait of Hormuz, and the size of the surplus that could emerge once disrupted barrels return." OIL CAPACITY REVIEW IN FOCUS The seven members have been boosting output targets for much of 2026 and in September completed the phased rollback of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in 2023. At earlier meetings, they kept the targets steady for October and November. OPEC+ still has one more layer of production cuts of about 2 million bpd covering most members through the end of 2026. The group needs to complete a review of members' production capacity during the fourth quarter before setting the 2027 baselines that will determine future quotas and shape plans to unwind those cuts, sources have said. The Iran war has disrupted projects to expand capacity across the Middle East, throwing estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, Reuters reported in October. As a result, the review is now expected to be completed by mid-November. (Writing by Alex Lawler; Editing by Joe Bavier and Alex Richardson)

Source: Reuters

FAST

SOFIA: Bulgarians went to the polls on Sunday (Nov 1) to elect a president after a tight race between the two leading candidates failed to produce an outright winner in last weekend's first round vote for the largely ceremonial role. Incumbent president, Iliana Iotova, 61, led over ex-caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, but fell short of the 50 per cent threshold in the first round race of 27 candidates that saw a record-low turnout. Exit polls will be published after voting ends at 8 pm (1800 GMT), with a result likely on Monday as the ballot papers are counted. The presidential vote comes against the backdrop of a series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast in the past month, which have sparked international condemnation and concerns about the growing reach of the war in Ukraine.

About two dozen seafarers are feared dead and the strikes have prompted the government to seek allied assistance to bolster maritime security. On Wednesday a Greek container ship sank after being hit by sea drones. Both leading presidential candidates have condemned the attacks. Prime Minister Rumen Radev, who backs Iotova, said the strikes' outcome "benefits the Russian Federation". They have both called for a diplomatic end to the war. A victory for Iotova would make her Bulgaria's first elected female president. She became acting president in January after Radev resigned to enter and win a parliamentary race on what many political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ticket. Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is supported by pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine. He signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv during his time as premier. A host of right-leaning political figures, among them ex-premier Boiko Borisov, have expressed support for Gyurov.

BEIJING, Nov 1 : Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi said on Sunday it delivered more than 50,000 electric vehicles in October, the highest monthly total this year, as it ramps up production to meet its 2026 target. Deliveries reached about 336,000 vehicles for the first 10 months after topping 30,000 units in August and 40,000 in September. The company aims to deliver 550,000 vehicles in 2026. Its January-October deliveries represent about 61 per cent of that goal.

item.title: BRICS+ Payments System Feasible, Common Currency Faces Hurdles, Report Says
item.description: BRICS+ countries should press ahead with a joint cross-border payments mechanism to reduce reliance on the U.S. dollar, but a shared currency would face major economic and institutional obstacles, a think tank report said on Friday. The paper, published by non-profit policy platform BRICS+ Thinking, …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
BRICS+ countries should press ahead with a joint cross-border payments mechanism to reduce reliance on the U.S. dollar, but a shared currency would face major economic and institutional obstacles, a think tank report said on Friday.

The paper, published by non-profit policy platform BRICS+ Thinking, urged the expanded grouping of major emerging economies led by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa to commit to such a mechanism and take the steps needed to make it work.

“It is absolutely crucial that their central banks embrace this goal and make sure that all the technical requirements are put in place to allow this mechanism to function,” said authors Gregory T. Chin, Danny Quah and Jim O’Neill, the former Goldman Sachs economist who coined the BRICS acronym.

Cross-border payments have long been on the BRICS agenda, though efforts to integrate members’ financial infrastructure have made limited progress.
